name: term_neonate_1h
description: Reference values for term_neonate_1h: the term_neonate_72h baby 71 h younger. RULE (user, 2026-11-05): a 1 h target is the 72 h target times the change between ~1 h and ~72 h measured WITHIN one longitudinal study (same cohort, same method); without such a pair the 72 h value is kept; absolute values only where the 72 h baby has no counterpart (the open duct). Other cohorts' absolute 12 h values are cross-checks in the notes. Grades: A = within-study pair, healthy term, at the ages; B = within-study pair with interpolation or an age proxy (48 h, 96 h) or two studies disagreeing; C = no pair (72 h kept), derived or carried.
state: calm, quiet awake or asleep, dressed/skin-to-skin at room temperature
compiled: 2026-11-06 (72 h x within-study change, as term_neonate_12h / _24h; user-accepted exceptions noted per row)

variables.label: Mixed venous O2 saturation (right heart, before the duct)
variables.notes: USER DECISION 2026-11-05: judged at the right heart, as the 72 h source measured it (van der Hoeven 1996, right-atrial fibre-optic catheter). The 72 h value is kept (no within-study pair). With a left-to-right duct the pulmonary artery carries oxygenated aortic blood, so it reads higher than the systemic venous return (at a shunt of ~45 mL/kg/min: RA 76.9, PA 80.9); at 72 h, duct closed, RA = PA. No within-study pair; the 72 h value is kept. Cross-check: Wolfsberger 2023: peripheral extraction constant over the first 24 h. The earlier 12 h row (78, brown-fat derivation 2026-10-27) had no within-study pair.

derivation.method: no within-study 12 h / 72 h pair: 72 h value kept

variables.label: Ductal net left-to-right flow
variables.method: LV output minus systemic flow; orifice physics
variables.notes: USER DECISION 2026-11-06: net left-to-right 70 (60-80). Drayton 1987 (10 term, volumetric Doppler): 62 (43-82) shortly after birth. Within-study LVO excess at 1 h, assuming the 72 h systemic flow: Agata 1994 +41 % -> ~81, Agata 1991 +33 % -> ~65; organ flows are lower at 1 h, so the shunt share of the excess is if anything larger.

derivation.method: USER DECISION 2026-11-06: net L->R 60-80

variables.notes: No within-study pair; the 72 h value is kept.

variables.label: Ductal diameter
variables.range_type: Kang 2 h and Agata 1 h, mean +/- 2SD spans
variables.notes: Agata 1994: 5.1 +/- 0.9 mm at 1 h; Kang 2016: 4.60 +/- 0.59 at 2 h. The pulmonary-end protrusion has started in only 30 % at 1 h (Hiraishi 1987): a wide, unrestrictive duct.

variables.label: Ductal right-to-left time
variables.notes: Bidirectional in all at 1-2 h (Agata 1994, Kang 2016), left-to-right dominant; right-to-left in early systole (Rudolph). van Laere 2018: R->L < 30 % of the cycle = bidirectional / growing.

variables.label: Ductal peak L->R velocity
variables.method: PW/CW Doppler at the pulmonary end
variables.notes: Peak left-to-right velocity in a wide bidirectional duct is low: Mandorla 1990 1.5 +/- 0.7 at the first exam (< 6 h); Ha 2018 1.43 (1.07-1.78) over 0-12 h.

variables.label: Ductal end-diastolic L->R velocity
variables.method: Bernoulli from the aorta-PA diastolic gradient
variables.model_readout: beat minimum of Pda.velocity_doppler (a dip would show here)
variables.notes: Reference only at 1 h: with right-to-left flow in early systole the beat minimum is the right-to-left peak (negative).

variables.label: Ductal peak / end-diastolic velocity
variables.notes: Reference only at 1 h (bidirectional: the peak/minimum ratio is not a restriction index).
